learning: Across ten races, the geometry and controller tested show that the best measured design is the iteration 1 reference. Line loss (about 1 per run) remains the unresolved failure mode, and line-loss search direction is the untested controller lever.
notes: Final robot: the iteration 1 reference geometry and controller exactly, reproduced in iterations 4, 6 and 10 at 69.3241. Any gain from an untested change is unmeasured, so none is made.
rationale: This is the final iteration, and the final unseen-track race is scored on the design delivered here, so the aim is the most reliable robot, not an untested improvement. The evidence is consistent. The geometry (five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m, y = 0.05 m, with wheel, body and mass unchanged) and the controller from iteration 1 (base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, last_direction, weights -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) scored 69.3241 in iterations 1, 4, 6 and 10, so the result is reproducible. Every single change tested away from this design lowered the score: 16 mm footprint (54.45, iteration 2), y = 0.03 m (59.64, iteration 3), the ±0.04 m span (52.47, iteration 5), base_speed 1.15 (61.77, iteration 7), kd 0.4 (56.44, iteration 8) and kd 0.2 (63.59, iteration 9). Line loss has stayed at about 1 per run (1.0 to 1.65) under every design, and steering oscillation (0.07 to 0.15) is not limiting. Untested levers (line-loss search direction, wheel_track, mass) have no line-loss evidence behind them. With no iterations remaining, an untested change would be a gamble on the final score. I therefore deliver the reference robot exactly. Sign check: sensors at positive x (left) carry positive weights, so a line on the left steers left, as the contract requires. Expected result: a score near 69.3 on the development tracks and a finish-or-off-track outcome on the unseen track that is not yet known. This is a prediction, not a measurement.
